brief:
WHAT HAPPENED
- An attack on an airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh killed 12 people and injured 300; Saudi and US officials blamed Yemen's Houthis, who have not commented.
- Donald Trump announced a deal for Russian diesel to address high fuel prices, drawing sharp condemnation from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
- Nvidia-backed data centre firm Firmus cancelled its initial public offering (IPO), citing recent market volatility and prevailing market conditions.
- The White House barred Microsoft from an international visa programme used by US tech companies to hire highly skilled foreign workers.
- High Street chain Boots was sold to a Canadian billionaire family.

WHY IT MATTERS
- Withdrawing an IPO—an initial public offering, which is when a private company first sells shares to the public on a stock exchange—reflects growing investor wariness over AI business valuations.
- Sourcing fuel from Russia highlights intense political urgency to curb consumer energy costs, even at the cost of diplomatic friction with allies.
- Policy restrictions on foreign worker programmes create direct operational constraints for large technology companies seeking specialised talent.

WHAT TO WATCH TODAY
- Any statement or response from Yemen's Houthis regarding the Riyadh airport strike.
- Continued geopolitical fallout and official statements between Washington, Kyiv, and Moscow regarding the diesel arrangement.
- Follow-up details on how the White House's foreign worker restriction on Microsoft will be enforced.
- Strategic plans and leadership announcements from Boots' new Canadian owners.

IN SIMPLE TERMS
Global security, trade, and corporate moves led today's news. A fatal airport attack occurred in Saudi Arabia, and a contentious US deal for Russian diesel drew pushback from Ukraine. Meanwhile, British chain Boots changed ownership, an Nvidia-backed data firm abandoned its planned stock market debut due to turbulent market conditions, and Microsoft was blocked by the White House from using a key visa programme to hire specialised foreign workers.
